NVDA.rationale: NVIDIA delivered a blowout Q1 FY2027 with revenue of $81.6B (+85% YoY, +43% QoQ), EPS of $2.39 (+215% YoY), and net income of $58.3B, all well above consensus. Gross margins held at ~75%, operating cash flow surged to $50.3B, and the balance sheet remains fortress-like with only $8.5B debt against $195B equity. The company guided Q2 revenue to $91B (vs. ~$87B consensus), announced an $80B additional buyback authorization, and raised its dividend 25x. Data center revenue of $75.2B (+92% YoY) continues to dominate at ~92% of total sales. Valuation has compressed meaningfully: the P/E of 33.5x is at the low end of its 33.5-66.8x 12-month range, and P/B of 27.4x is near the bottom of its 27.4-57.9x range, representing a significant discount to the stock's own history despite accelerating earnings. However, several risks temper the score: (1) competition from hyperscaler custom chips (Amazon Trainium, Google TPU) is real and growing, with Amazon's CEO noting AWS is deploying more Trainium than Nvidia chips; (2) China market is effectively lost with no data center compute revenue assumed in guidance; (3) the semiconductor trade is at 73% crowding per BofA's survey, the highest on record; (4) rising Treasury yields (10Y at 4.57%) and inflation (CPI 3.8%, PPI 6%) create macro headwinds for mega-cap tech valuations; (5) post-earnings stock reaction was muted (-0.5%), continuing a pattern of declining post-earnings pops. The near-term catalyst of the earnings beat and strong guidance has already been delivered, limiting further re-rating potential in the immediate term. Net: excellent fundamentals and trajectory with meaningful valuation improvement vs. history, but competitive and macro headwinds cap the upside.

Nvidia posted adjusted earnings of $1.87 per share for the first quarter, higher than the $1.76 analysts were looking for. Revenue jumped 85% year-over-year to a record $81.6 billion. Current-quarter revenue was seen rocketing to $91 billion.
Nvidia's stock sank following the analyst call, on track for a fourth-straight post-earnings slide. $80 billion buyback and upping dividend. Guidance beats estimates.
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy revealed that AWS is deploying more Trainium chips than Nvidia chips and has a $225 billion backlog for Trainium compute.

Bank of America's May Global Fund Manager Survey reveals that 73% of professional investors now view 'long global semiconductors' as the most crowded trade on Wall Street, up from 24% in April—the steepest one-month jump on record.

Culper Research released a short report alleging that Nvidia has a significant undisclosed 'China problem,' claiming over 20% of its FY 2026 compute revenues come from Chinese demand through illegal diversions via Southeast Asian intermediaries.
NVIDIA controls an estimated 88 percent to 92 percent of the high-end data center GPU market. Gross margins remain near 75 percent.

As of the end of fiscal year 2026, we were effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center computing/compute market, and our effective foreclosure from the China market helped our competitors build larger developer and customer ecosystems to challenge us worldwide.
